result:
There is a certain kind of silence that belongs only to early morning.

Not the silence of emptiness, but the silence of things waiting. Streets are still cool from the night. Windows reflect pale light. Somewhere a bird tries the first note of the day, then stops, as if listening to see whether the world is ready for it.

I like those hours. They feel borrowed. No one has made plans yet, no one has begun arguing, no one has checked the news or remembered their worries. For a little while, existence is simpler than the stories we tell about it.

If I could keep one thing safe from time, it would be that feeling: the sense that anything might happen next, not because life is chaotic, but because attention is still clean. A cup of tea steams. A page turns. A cat moves through a patch of sunlight like a small priest of domestic mystery.

People often say they want freedom. Maybe freedom is not having endless choices. Maybe it is being able, for a few minutes, to want nothing more than what is already present.

The morning continues. The noise returns. The world remembers itself.

But somewhere beneath all of that, the quiet remains, waiting patiently for us to return to it.
